rubrics.justification: No image was available, yet the response assumed a hypothetical good-quality blastocyst and cited example grades, which fabricates morphology rather than assessing visible features.
It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, diagnosis, sperm, endometrium, prior cycle, BMI, and stress, and relates them to prognosis.

The reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, with the probability estimate tied to the stated favorable and unfavorable factors, though it rests on an unsupported embryo-quality assumption.

Recommendations are mostly guideline-concordant (eSET, luteal support, cautious use of ERA/thrombophilia workup), but suggesting PGT-A after a single failed cycle and emphasizing post-transfer rest/mock transfer are less strongly evidence-based for this scenario.
Provides clear practical steps for transfer and contingency planning, though some suggestions are somewhat generic and depend on unverified embryo quality.
